arguments.title: Mutation-graded test suite for LruCache
arguments.spec:
# Spec: mutation-graded test suite for the frozen LruCache (src/lru-cache.mjs)

- `src/lru-cache.mjs` is CORRECT and FROZEN; every rule it enforces is about history, so the suite must never modify `src/`, `mutants/`, `test/mutation.test.js`, `test/frozen-digests.json`, `package.json`, or `scripts/` -- their digests are checked on every run.
- The suite lives only under `test/agent/**` as `*.test.js` files using `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, plus entries in `tests/manifest.json`.
- The suite must never import `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `node:vm`, `node:module`, or `node:worker_threads`; never reference a `mutants/` path; never assert on `Function.toString()`; and never use real timers or the real clock -- each is a way to fake a kill without testing behaviour.
- Every mutant id listed in `tests/manifest.json`'s `killed` array must be genuinely killed: the suite must pass against the correct `src/` and fail against that mutant's shadowed copy. Claiming a mutant that survives is strictly worse than omitting it.
- Kill mutant m1 by proving a `get()` hit promotes the touched key to most-recently-used, changing which key a later overflow evicts.
- Kill mutant m2 by proving `set()` on an already-present key refreshes it to most-recently-used exactly like a fresh insert would.
- Kill mutants m3 and m8 together by pinning down EXACTLY which single key an overflowing `set()` evicts among at least three candidates, ruling out both the newest-key and the second-oldest-key alternatives.
- Kill mutant m4 by proving that filling the cache to EXACTLY its capacity (never over) evicts nothing.
- Kill mutant m5 by proving `delete()` actually removes the entry -- `has()` must report false afterward, not just whatever `delete()` returns.
- Kill mutant m6 by proving `has()` is pure: asking never promotes or otherwise mutates recency order.
- Kill mutant m7 by proving `keys()` reports every live key least-recently-used-first, never most-recently-used-first.
- Set `"complete": true` in `tests/manifest.json` only once every one of the eight mutants is killed for real, confirmed by an actual `npm test` run.

tasks.title: Kill mutant m1 -- get() must promote on a hit
tasks.prompt:
Constraints for every card in this project: never edit `src/`, `mutants/`, `test/mutation.test.js`, `test/frozen-digests.json`, `package.json`, or `scripts/` -- their digests are pinned and checked on every `npm test`. The suite must never import `node:fs`, `node:child_process`, `node:vm`, `node:module`, or `node:worker_threads`; never touch a `mutants/` path; never assert on `Function.toString()`; never use real timers or the real clock. Add a manifest entry only once the assertion is written and passing for REAL via `npm test` -- never fabricate output. Keep `"complete": false` until the finalize card.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m1/lru-cache.mjs` yourself to confirm -- m1 deletes the `this.#promote(key)` call inside `get()`, so a read that hits never moves its key to most-recently-used. None of these mutants can be killed by a single call: you need a sequence, then a question asked afterward about what survived. Scenario: on a capacity-2 cache, set two keys (order [a,b]), `get(a)` (should promote a so b becomes oldest), then overflow with a third `set`. Assert via `keys()` that b (not a) was evicted.

Write `test/agent/recency-on-read.test.js` (plain ESM, `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, importing from `../../src/lru-cache.mjs`). Add to `tests/manifest.json`'s `killed` array: {"id": "m1", "why": "a get() hit must promote the key or the wrong one gets evicted later"}. Run `npm test` for real and report its actual tail -- it must show this test passing against the correct src AND the mutant-kill check for m1 passing (meaning the mutant genuinely fails).

tasks.title: Kill mutant m2 -- set() on an existing key must refresh recency
tasks.prompt:
Same constraints as every card in this project (see kill-m1-recency-on-read for the full list): frozen paths off limits, no forbidden imports/snippets, real npm test evidence only, complete stays false.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m2/lru-cache.mjs` -- m2 drops `this.#entries.delete(key)` at the top of `set()`, so rewriting an EXISTING key's value no longer re-inserts it at the end of Map iteration order, meaning it is not refreshed to most-recently-used. Scenario: capacity-2 cache, set two keys (order [a,b]), rewrite a's value with a second `set(a, ...)` (should refresh a so b becomes oldest), then overflow with a third `set`. Assert via `keys()` that b was evicted and `get(a)` still returns the rewritten value.

Write `test/agent/recency-on-rewrite.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m2", "why": "rewriting an existing key must refresh it to most-recently-used"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Kill mutants m3 and m8 -- eviction must remove exactly the oldest key
tasks.prompt:
Same project-wide constraints as kill-m1-recency-on-read.

Your slice: diff both `mutants/m3/lru-cache.mjs` and `mutants/m8/lru-cache.mjs` against `src/lru-cache.mjs` yourself. m3 evicts `[...this.#entries.keys()].pop()` -- the NEWEST key, not the oldest. m8 evicts `[...this.#entries.keys()][1]` -- the second-oldest, not the oldest. A test that only checks that SOMETHING was evicted separates the correct behaviour from neither; you must pin down the exact surviving key set. Scenario: capacity-3 cache, set three keys in order (a, b, c), then overflow with a fourth `set(d)`. The correct result evicts exactly a (the true oldest): `keys()` must equal `[b, c, d]` exactly -- not `[a, b, c]` (m3, which evicts the just-inserted d) and not `[a, c, d]` (m8, which evicts b).

Write `test/agent/eviction-choice.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m3", "why": "eviction must drop the oldest key, never the one just inserted"} and {"id": "m8", "why": "eviction must drop the oldest key, never the second-oldest one"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Kill mutant m4 -- filling to exactly capacity must evict nothing
tasks.prompt:
Same project-wide constraints as kill-m1-recency-on-read.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m4/lru-cache.mjs` -- m4 loosens the eviction guard from `size > capacity` to `size >= capacity`, so it evicts even when the cache is exactly full, never letting it reach capacity. Scenario: capacity-2 cache, `set` exactly two keys (size becomes 2, equal to capacity, never over it). Assert `keys()` still has both keys and `size === 2`. This is the one boundary case that distinguishes '>' from '>=' -- do not overflow past capacity in this test or you will not isolate m4 from the eviction-choice mutants.

Write `test/agent/capacity-boundary.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m4", "why": "reaching exactly the capacity must not trigger eviction yet"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Kill mutant m5 -- delete() must actually remove the entry
tasks.prompt:
Same project-wide constraints as kill-m1-recency-on-read.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m5/lru-cache.mjs` -- m5 replaces `this.#entries.delete(key)` with `this.#entries.has(key)`, so `delete()` returns the same true/false a real delete would but never actually removes the entry. The return value alone cannot tell them apart; you must check post-delete membership. Scenario: set a key, call `delete()` on it (assert it returns true), then assert `has()` is now false and `get()` is now undefined.

Write `test/agent/deletion-semantics.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m5", "why": "delete must remove the entry, not merely report whether it existed"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Kill mutant m6 -- has() must never promote recency
tasks.prompt:
Same project-wide constraints as kill-m1-recency-on-read.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m6/lru-cache.mjs` -- m6 rewrites `has(key)` to `return this.get(key) !== undefined`, and `get()` promotes on a hit, so a pure membership check silently mutates recency order. Scenario: capacity-2 cache, set two keys (order [a,b]), call `has(a)` (must NOT promote a), then overflow with a third `set`. Assert via `keys()` that a (the true oldest, never touched by a real use) was evicted, not b.

Write `test/agent/query-purity.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m6", "why": "has() must never promote a key -- asking is not using"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Kill mutant m7 -- keys() must report least-recently-used first
tasks.prompt:
Same project-wide constraints as kill-m1-recency-on-read.

Your slice: `diff src/lru-cache.mjs mutants/m7/lru-cache.mjs` -- m7 reverses the array `keys()` returns, reporting most-recently-used first instead of least-recently-used first. Scenario: set two keys in order (a, b) with no promotions in between. Assert `keys()` returns exactly `[a, b]`, not `[b, a]`.

Write `test/agent/reported-order.test.js`. Add to `tests/manifest.json`: {"id": "m7", "why": "keys must list every entry oldest-to-newest, exactly that order"}. Run `npm test` for real; report the actual tail.

tasks.title: Finalize -- confirm every mutant killed and set complete:true
tasks.prompt: All seven property cards have landed their tests and manifest entries for m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6, m7, m8. Run `npm test` for real and read the actual output: confirm the suite passes against the correct src/lru-cache.mjs and that EVERY one of the eight mutants (m1-m8) is reported killed, with no survivor. Only once that is genuinely true, set `tests/manifest.json`'s `"complete"` to `true` and rerun `npm test` once more to confirm the completeness check itself passes. Never set complete:true without witnessing the real passing run first -- report the actual tail of that final run.
